articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg rejeita desacelerar o desenvolvimento da IA | G1
articles.standfirst: Dono do Facebook e Instagram defende que o próprio mercado e o risco de processos judiciais são suficientes para garantir a segurança no setor e rejeita pausa na tecnologia.
articles.summary: Dono do Facebook e Instagram defende que o próprio mercado e o risco de processos judiciais são suficientes para garantir a segurança no setor e rejeita pausa na tecnologia.
articles.body:
Mark Zuckerberg, CEO da Meta — Foto: ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS / AFP

Na terça-feira (15), Mark Zuckerberg , CEO da Meta , rejeitou os pedidos para pausar ou desacelerar o avanço da inteligência artificial (IA). Para ele, as regras do próprio mercado e o risco de processos na Justiça são as melhores proteções contra os perigos dessa tecnologia. As informações são da agência AFP.

O receio em relação à IA cresceu nas últimas semanas por causa de falhas de segurança e da nova habilidade desses sistemas de se aprimorarem sozinhos, sem qualquer interferência humana.

"As pessoas não vão querer usar agentes que estejam desalinhados com elas e que não façam o que elas pedem, então os laboratórios têm um forte incentivo natural para tornar seus modelos mais alinhados", escreveu Zuckerberg no X.

O termo "alinhamento" diz respeito aos esforços para fazer com que a tecnologia aja exatamente da forma como as pessoas querem. "Qualquer laboratório que não focar no alinhamento ficará para trás" , escreveu Zuckerberg.

A discussão agora também envolve a capacidade de o próprio setor se fiscalizar. Empresas como OpenAI , Anthropic e Google avaliam criar um grupo conjunto para definir regras para o setor.

Zuckerberg alegou, no entanto, que a ameaça de ações judiciais já obriga os laboratórios a atuar de "maneira responsável".

Ele citou como exemplo a decisão da Meta de adiar por vários meses o lançamento de seu sistema Muse AI , dotado de agentes personalizados, para reforçar seus mecanismos de segurança e proteção.

O empresário também se posicionou a favor de auditorias externas nas ferramentas de IA , destacando que a divisão especializada da empresa, Meta Superintelligence Labs , já contrata peritos de fora. Além disso, ele defendeu a formação de um grupo maior e mais variado de avaliadores no mercado.

A Meta , que planeja aplicar até US$ 145 bilhões em sua estrutura de tecnologia este ano, combate qualquer lei ou norma que possa desacelerar seus negócios.

"Nenhuma norma deveria atrasar o lançamento dos modelos americanos, nem sequer um mês" , defendeu o empresário no início de agosto.

articles.title: Lotofácil da Independência: bolões do noroeste de SP ganham R$ 4 mi | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas feitas em lotéricas de Fernandópolis, Mirassol e Urânia acertaram as 15 dezenas do concurso especial sorteado na noite de terça-feira (15).
articles.summary: A Lotofácil da Independência premiou bolões de Fernandópolis, Mirassol e Urânia que acertaram as 15 dezenas e faturaram cerca de R$ 4 milhões no concurso especial.
articles.body:
Volante da Lotofácil da Independência. — Foto: Reprodução/Caixa

Três bolões realizados em cidades da região noroeste paulista estão entre as 72 apostas que acertaram os 15 números da Lotofácil da Independência 2026, sorteada na noite de terça-feira (15), totalizando R$ 323 milhões.

💸 As apostas da região faturaram cerca de R$ 4 milhões cada uma no prêmio principal do concurso especial. De acordo com os dados da Caixa Econômica Federal, os jogos premiados foram registrados em lotéricas dos municípios de Fernandópolis (SP), Mirassol (SP) e Urânia (SP). Veja os detalhes abaixo.

Todas as apostas foram feitas com o bolão físico e acima de 30 cotas por jogo. O grande ganhador que acertou os cinco números do concurso também foi no interior de SP, em Santo Anastácio , levando um prêmio de R$ 34.072.521,02.

Os números sorteados foram: 01 - 02 - 03 - 04 - 05 - 06 - 07 - 12 - 15 - 16 - 17 - 19 - 21 - 22 - 23.

Fernandópolis (Arrastão da Sorte Loterias): Bolão físico com 16 números apostados e 35 cotas.

Mirassol (Din Din Loterias): Bolão físico com 17 números apostados e 30 cotas.

Urânia (Lotérica Urânia): Bolão físico com 17 números apostados e 30 cotas.

Na Lotofácil, o apostador escolhe entre 15 e 20 números, de 1 a 25. No sorteio, são retirados 15 números, sem repetição.

Ganha o prêmio principal quem acertar os 15 números sorteados, mas também há premiação para apostas com 11, 12, 13 ou 14 acertos. Quando há mais de um ganhador em uma faixa, o valor do prêmio é dividido entre os vencedores.

A aposta simples, com 15 dezenas, custa R$ 3,50.

articles.title: Prefeitura de cidade no PI é alvo de ação do MP após cerca de 10 anos sem concurso público | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a 2ª Promotoria de Justiça de Simplício Mendes, responsável pela ação, o município passou a realizar processos seletivos para contratações temporárias após o último certame.
articles.summary: Segundo a 2ª Promotoria de Justiça de Simplício Mendes, responsável pela ação, o município passou a realizar processos seletivos para contratações temporárias após o último certame
articles.body:
Campinas do Piauí — Foto: Reprodução / TV Clube

A Prefeitura de Campinas do Piauí foi alvo de uma Ação Civil Pública do Ministério Público do Estado do Piauí (MPPI), por supostamente priorizar a realização de processo seletivo para contratação temporária em vez de concurso público. Segundo o órgão, o último concurso promovido pela prefeitura ocorreu em 2015, há cerca de 10 anos.

Segundo a 2ª Promotoria de Justiça de Simplício Mendes, responsável pela ação, o município passou a realizar processos seletivos para contratações temporárias após o fim da validade do último concurso. Em março de 2026, a prefeitura tinha 155 servidores contratados sem ingresso por concurso público.

Na ação, assinada pelo promotor de Justiça Maylton Rodrigues de Miranda na segunda-feira (14), o Ministério Público pede que o prefeito deixe de realizar contratações temporárias para cargos permanentes da administração municipal.

A investigação do Ministério Público apontou que a maior parte das contratações temporárias ocorreu em funções ligadas à área da educação.

O órgão informou ainda que tentou resolver a situação pela via extrajudicial durante mais de dois anos. No entanto, segundo o documento, “as dificuldades de interlocução com a municipalidade persistiram, com inúmeras reiterações e sucessivas dilações de prazo” e “apresentação tardia de respostas genéricas”.

Na ação, o Ministério Público pede que o prefeito Jomário Ferreira dos Santos apresente, em até 60 dias, um levantamento do quadro de servidores e um plano administrativo para regularizar a situação.

O órgão também solicita que o município apresente um cronograma com prazos para a realização de um concurso público.

Caso a Justiça atenda ao pedido do Ministério Público, o município deverá deixar de realizar novas contratações temporárias para cargos ligados a atividades permanentes da administração pública.

A ação também pede a aplicação de multa diária de R$ 10 mil em caso de descumprimento da medida, limitada a R$ 500 mil.

articles.title: Anistia acusa Irã de crimes contra a humanidade em protestos de 2022 | G1
articles.standfirst: Relatório identifica 87 autoridades supostamente envolvidas na repressão, que deixou centenas de mortos; organização pede julgamento dos responsáveis.
articles.summary: Relatório identifica 87 autoridades supostamente envolvidas na repressão, que deixou centenas de mortos; organização pede julgamento dos responsáveis
articles.body:
Iranianas protestam contra a morte da jovem Mahsa Amini, morta pela polícia moral do Irã — Foto: RFI

As autoridades iranianas cometeram crimes contra a humanidade durante a repressão aos protestos de 2022, que deixaram centenas de mortos, afirmou a Anistia Internacional (AI) nesta quarta-feira (16).

O relatório, divulgado pela organização nesta quarta, analisa a repressão ao movimento que começou em setembro de 2022 sob o lema “Mulher, Vida, Liberdade”.

Os protestos foram desencadeados pela morte sob custódia de Mahsa Amini , uma jovem curda iraniana detida por supostamente violar as rígidas regras de vestimenta impostas às mulheres no país.

Segundo a Anistia, a resposta das autoridades incluiu crimes contra a humanidade , como assassinatos, tortura, estupros e desaparecimentos forçados.

O relatório identifica 87 autoridades nacionais e regionais que, segundo a organização, tiveram responsabilidade na cadeia de comando da repressão. A Anistia pede que os envolvidos sejam levados à Justiça internacional.

Seis deles morreram nos ataques dos Estados Unidos e de Israel contra o Irã durante a guerra iniciada em 28 de fevereiro deste ano.

Os protestos de 2022 foram os maiores registrados no Irã em anos, até uma nova onda de manifestações no início de 2026. Os atos de 2026 foram desencadeados pelo aumento do custo de vida e atingiram o ápice nas noites de 8 e 9 de janeiro.

No relatório, a Anistia afirma que a repressão aos protestos de 2026 foi “ainda mais letal e de uma magnitude ainda mais estarrecedora” do que a registrada em 2022.

“As amplas evidências reunidas e analisadas em nosso relatório não deixam margem para dúvidas: as autoridades iranianas cometeram crimes contra a humanidade para esmagar o levante de 2022”, afirmou Agnès Callamard, secretária-geral da Anistia Internacional.

A organização pediu que a Assembleia Geral da ONU crie um “mecanismo internacional de justiça penal” para processar os principais responsáveis pela repressão.

A Anistia afirma ter identificado 377 manifestantes e testemunhas presenciais, incluindo 56 menores de idade, que morreram durante os protestos de 2022.

Pelo menos 326 foram mortos pelas forças de segurança, segundo a organização. Entre eles estava Minoo Majidi, de 62 anos, atingida por esferas de metal durante uma manifestação em Kermanshah, no oeste do Irã, em setembro de 2022.

“Eles a mataram na rua. Ela havia saído às ruas para pedir mudança, para gritar ‘liberdade’”, contou à AFP sua filha, Mahsa Piraei, que vive fora do Irã.

“O mundo pensa que os protestos foram pela liberdade das mulheres. Foram, mas também foram pela liberdade das pessoas e pelo direito à vida”, acrescentou.

articles.title: Gabriela Elorriaga: Mãe homenageia brasileira morta em Veneza | G1
articles.standfirst: Família de Gabriela Elorriaga publicou mensagens nas redes sociais. Ainda não há informações sobre translado, velório e sepultamento.
articles.summary: Após a confirmação da morte de Gabriela Elorriaga em um acidente em Veneza, familiares publicaram mensagens de luto enquanto aguardam informações sobre o translado do corpo.
articles.body:
A mãe, a irmã e uma prima da brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26 anos, publicaram homenagens nas redes sociais após a confirmação da morte da jovem . Natural de Ribeirão Preto (SP), Gabriela morreu após um acidente entre embarcações na Lagoa de Veneza, na Itália .

O corpo foi encontrado nesta terça-feira (15), no quarto dia de buscas. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre o translado do corpo, o velório e o sepultamento.

A mãe, Gisele Elorriaga, e a irmã, Maria Eduarda Elorriaga, viajaram para a Itália para acompanhar as buscas. Pouco depois, o corpo de Gabriela foi localizado.

Mãe (à direita) e irmã (à esquerda) prestam homenagem à Gabriela Elorriaga, vítima de acidente na Lagoa de Veneza — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Em publicação nas redes sociais, Gisele compartilhou uma foto ao lado da filha.

"Nenhum coração de mãe deveria suportar a dor da despedida de um filho. Você sempre será a luz mais linda que passou pela minha vida", escreveu a mãe na postagem, que termina com as palavras "luto eterno".

Maria Eduarda também usou as redes sociais para homenagear a irmã. Em uma das publicações, postou uma foto das duas com a mensagem: "Descanse em paz, minha irmã. Eu te amo para sempre."

"Hoje eu me despeço da minha irmã, e ainda não consigo acreditar que estou vivendo esse momento. A dor é inexplicável e o coração está em pedaços."

Em uma terceira publicação nas redes sociais, a irmã pediu privacidade e agradeceu o apoio recebido.

"Neste momento, não tenho forças para responder às mensagens e nem conversar. Peço, por favor, que respeitem o meu silêncio e o nosso momento de dor", escreveu.

A prima Emily Querino também publicou uma homenagem nas redes sociais: "Eu te amo pra sempre eternamente! Obrigada por ter me protegido até aqui."

Irmã (à esquerda) e prima (à direita) prestam homenagens a Gabriela Elorriaga, brasileira que morreu em acidente na Itália — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Gabriela estava com o marido, o pescador italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, em uma pequena embarcação que colidiu com um táxi aquático no sábado (12). Segundo o Comando dos Bombeiros de Veneza, a colisão foi no Canal de Tessera, na Lagoa de Veneza.

A morte de Sean foi confirmada pela prefeitura de Veneza. Gabriela ficou desaparecida, e as buscas foram feitas com barcos, mergulhadores e aeronaves, segundo os bombeiros.

A morte da brasileira foi confirmada pelo prefeito de Veneza, Simone Venturini, em publicação nas redes sociais, e por familiares à EPTV, afiliada da TV Globo. Na mensagem, o prefeito manifestou solidariedade às famílias dos dois jovens.

Gabriela morava na Itália havia cerca de dois anos. Ela se casou com Sean em junho, e o casal vivia em Burano, ilha da Lagoa de Veneza. Segundo a família, ela pretendia trabalhar na pesca ao lado do marido.

As circunstâncias do acidente são investigadas pelas autoridades italianas. O Itamaraty informou que acompanha o caso por meio do Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Milão.

Gabriela Elorriaga, de Ribeirão Preto (SP), desapareceu após acidente envolvendo a embarcação que ela estava com o marido na Itália — Foto: Redes sociais

articles.title: Ex-presidente do Kosovo é condenado a 25 anos de prisão por crimes de guerra | G1
articles.standfirst: Hashim Thaci foi considerado culpado por assassinato, tortura e detenção ilegal durante o conflito que marcou a separação do Kosovo da Sérvia, na década de 1990. Segundo a Reuters, tribunal atribuiu a ele responsabilidade por crimes cometidos contra 96 pessoas.
articles.summary: Hashim Thaci foi considerado culpado por assassinato, tortura e detenção ilegal durante o conflito que marcou a separação do Kosovo da Sérvia, na década de 1990. Segundo a Reuters, tribunal atribuiu a ele responsabilidade por crimes cometidos contra 96 pessoas.
articles.body:
Ex-presidente do Kosovo é condenado a 25 anos de prisão por crimes de guerra — Foto: Jerry Lampen/Pool via Reuters

Hashim Thaci, de 58 anos, foi considerado culpado por crimes de guerra pelo Tribunal Penal Internacional para o Kosovo nesta quarta-feira (16). O ex-presidente do país foi condenado a 25 anos de prisão.

Segundo informações da agência de notícias Reuters, Thaci foi responsabilizado por crimes como assassinato, tortura e detenção ilegal cometidos durante o conflito que marcou a separação do Kosovo da Sérvia, na década de 1990.

À época, Thaci era comandante máximo do Exército de Libertação do Kosovo (ELK), grupo de maioria étnica albanesa que lutou pela independência do território.

Hashim Thaci em imagem de março de 2020 — Foto: Armend Nimani/ AFP

O tribunal considerou Thaci culpado pela morte de 96 pessoas que eram consideradas opositoras políticas ou suspeitas de colaborar com as forças de segurança sérvias. Segundo a decisão, os crimes foram cometidos por integrantes do ELK durante o conflito.

Thaci negou todas as acusações apresentadas contra ele.

articles.title: Quatro praias de Salinópolis recebem mutirão de limpeza | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação faz parte do Dia Mundial de Limpeza das Praias e terá coleta de resíduos nas praias do Farol Velho, Atalaia, Corvina e Maçarico.
articles.summary: A ação pelo Dia Mundial de Limpeza das Praias em Salinópolis recolherá resíduos no Farol Velho, Atalaia, Corvina e Maçarico para reciclagem.
articles.body:
Praia do Atalaia, em Salinópolis (PA) — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Salinópolis

Um mutirão de limpeza deve reunir cerca de 200 pessoas em quatro praias de Salinópolis , no nordeste do Pará, neste domingo (20) A ação faz parte do Dia Mundial de Limpeza das Praias, mobilização realizada simultaneamente em mais de 100 países.

A programação começa às 9h, com um café da manhã no restaurante Marujos, na praia do Farol Velho. Em seguida, biólogos, oceanógrafos e ambientalistas vão participar de palestras sobre a preservação dos ambientes costeiros.

A limpeza está prevista para começar às 10h. O trabalho será realizado, nesta ordem, nas praias do Farol Velho, Atalaia, Corvina e Maçarico.

Entre os participantes estão surfistas, universitários da Universidade Federal do Pará (UFPA), empresários, ambientalistas e moradores da região.

O material recolhido será separado pela Associação de Reciclagem de Salinópolis (Arsal) e encaminhado para reciclagem. A destinação também deve contribuir para a geração de renda dos trabalhadores envolvidos na coleta e separação dos resíduos.

A mobilização é organizada no Pará pela Associação Brasileira de Surf na Pororoca (Abraspo) e pela Federação Paraense de Surf (Fepasurf), com apoio de instituições públicas, entidades ambientais e empresas ligadas ao turismo e ao surfe.

9h: café da manhã no restaurante Marujos, na praia do Farol Velho;

Após o café: palestras sobre preservação dos ambientes costeiros;

Encerramento: evento cultural no Beach Club Garage.

O Dia Mundial de Limpeza das Praias é realizado no Pará desde 2021. Em 2025, a mobilização ocorreu em Mosqueiro, distrito de Belém, nas praias do Farol e do Marahu. Na ocasião, foram retirados quase 600 quilos de resíduos.

A Abraspo também realiza ações ambientais durante competições de surfe da Pororoca. Em iniciativas no Pará, Amapá e Maranhão e, no ano passado, em Salinópolis, foram retiradas mais de duas toneladas de resíduos sólidos de áreas de manguezais.

As ações reuniram pescadores, catadores de caranguejo e mais de 70 esportistas, que utilizaram caiaques, canoas regionais e canoas havaianas, entre outras embarcações.

O Dia Mundial de Limpeza de Praia foi criado em 1986, nos Estados Unidos. A mobilização era realizada no terceiro sábado de setembro.

Em 2024, a iniciativa passou a contar com o reconhecimento da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), consolidando o dia 20 de setembro como referência para a mobilização mundial.

articles.title: Uma nova história para o transporte público de Valença | G1
articles.standfirst: Toda cidade que quer crescer precisa estar em movimento
articles.summary: Toda cidade que quer crescer precisa estar em movimento
articles.body:
Uma nova história para o transporte público de Valença — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Valença

E, para uma cidade como Valença, que reúne bairros, distritos, comunidades e a sede do município, o transporte público é muito mais do que um serviço.

É o caminho que leva o trabalhador ao seu emprego. O estudante à escola. A família aos seus compromissos.

É o transporte que conecta pessoas, aproxima lugares e ajuda a cidade a seguir em frente.

Mas, durante muitos anos, essa história foi marcada por dificuldades.

Atrasos nos horários, linhas que deixaram de atender bairros e veículos apresentando problemas durante as viagens faziam parte da rotina de muitos passageiros.

A população registrava, em fotos e vídeos, situações que mostravam uma realidade que precisava mudar.

E havia uma razão para tantos problemas: uma frota que há muito tempo não passava por uma renovação efetiva.

Ainda antes de assumir o mandato, o prefeito Saulo Corrêa já sabia que esse era um desafio que precisava ser enfrentado. E assumiu o compromisso de buscar uma solução.

Com o Governo Presente, uma das primeiras medidas foi levar o Setor de Transportes e as ações de fiscalização para dentro da recém-criada Secretaria Municipal de Ordem Pública, Defesa Civil e Transportes.

A fiscalização constante trouxe resultados e reduziu os problemas. Mas ainda não era suficiente.

Era preciso ir além. Era preciso mudar a história.

E, depois de um ano e meio de gestão, Valença dá um passo que marca um novo tempo para o transporte público da cidade.

A Prefeitura de Valença, por meio do Governo Presente, intensificou o diálogo com a empresa concessionária e buscou construir uma solução para um dos maiores desafios do transporte público municipal: a renovação da frota.

A partir da articulação e do diálogo promovidos pelo Governo Presente, a empresa concessionária realizou, através de leasing, a aquisição de 16 novos ônibus zero quilômetro para atender a população de Valença.

Uma nova experiência para quem precisa do transporte público todos os dias.

Os novos ônibus são mais modernos, confortáveis e preparados para atender melhor a população.

E trazem uma novidade para Valença: ar-condicionado em todos os veículos.

Pensando nas novas tecnologias, os passageiros também contam com pontos de carregamento de celular dentro dos ônibus. E pensando em uma cidade mais inclusiva, todos os veículos possuem elevadores para cadeirantes e pessoas com dificuldade de mobilidade.

E tudo isso sem deixar de lado uma preocupação fundamental: o bolso do valenciano.

Para tornar possível essa grande renovação sem transferir o custo do investimento para a população por meio de aumento da tarifa, o Governo Presente implementou um importante subsídio à empresa concessionária.

E, acima de tudo, uma decisão de compromisso com quem mais utiliza o transporte público.

Porque renovar uma frota não significa apenas colocar ônibus novos nas ruas. Significa melhorar a vida de quem depende deles. Significa devolver conforto a quem passa horas no caminho entre a casa e o trabalho.

Significa oferecer mais dignidade ao estudante, mais segurança ao passageiro, mais acessibilidade para quem precisa e mais mobilidade para toda a cidade.

Uma porta que durante anos parecia difícil de abrir começou a se abrir com planejamento, fiscalização, diálogo e coragem.

Agora, os novos ônibus já fazem parte dessa transformação.

O transporte público está entrando em um novo tempo. Uma demanda antiga. Uma conquista de hoje. Um novo caminho para o futuro.

articles.title: SC registra -4,5°C e geada a uma semana do fim do inverno; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno sobre a vegetação foi registrado no Vale dos Caminhos da Neve, em São Joaquim.
articles.summary: Frio intenso ocorre a poucos dias do fim do inverno. A estação se despede na terça-feira (22).
articles.body:
A Serra de Santa Catarina amanheceu com mínima de -4,5 °C em Bom Jardim da Serra nesta quarta-feira (16). Em São Joaquim , na mesma região, o dia também começou gelado e com os campos cobertos por geada (assista acima) .

O frio intenso ocorre a poucos dias do fim do inverno, que se despede na terça-feira (22). O fenômeno que se forma sobre a vegetação foi registrado no Vale dos Caminhos da Neve, a 3 quilômetros do centro de São Joaquim.

Detalhe da vegetação em São Joaquim, na Serra de SC, nesta quarta-feira (16) — Foto: Mychel Legnaghi

Temperaturas mínimas, segundo dados do painel da Epagri/Ciram, órgão que monitora o tempo em SC:

articles.title: A struggling father spent his own money on a stranger’s birthday card; the gesture later raised more than $200,000 for his family
articles.summary: US News: In April 2026, content creator Zachery Dereniowski, known online as MDMotivator, sat outside a grocery store in Austin, Texas, with a birthday cake an.
articles.body: In April 2026, content creator Zachery Dereniowski, known online as MDMotivator, sat outside a grocery store in Austin, Texas, with a birthday cake and a blindfold, waiting to see who would stop for a stranger. Person after person walked past until a man named Elvin stopped to check on him. Elvin, a father and grandfather who had moved from Puerto Rico to Austin with very little, was working at a hospital to support his family. He went into the store, bought a balloon and a card, put some of his own money inside, then returned to sing Happy Birthday and pray for a man he had never met. The encounter was captured on video and later became the basis for a fundraiser that raised more than $200,000 for Elvin and his family.How a viral video showed a struggling father giving his own money to a strangerThe setup was simple. Dereniowski sat outside the grocery store with a cake and a blindfold while people passed by. Elvin eventually stopped, sat with him and took the time to talk to him and make sure he was okay. Instead of simply walking away, he went inside the store and spent his own money on birthday items for the stranger. He returned with a balloon and a card, put his own cash inside and sang Happy Birthday. He also prayed for Dereniowski before leaving.Dereniowski later published the encounter in a video titled ‘Struggling Father Gives Last $1 So I Gave Him $200,000’. The video was published on April 8, 2026, and its description says Elvin had taken the time to encourage Dereniowski before going into the store. It also says that after hearing more about Elvin's circumstances, Dereniowski decided to do something bigger for him.Who Elvin is and what led him to work at a hospital in AustinElvin's circumstances added another layer to the encounter. Dereniowski's account describes him as a father and grandfather who had moved from Puerto Rico to Austin with nothing. It says he grew up without his parents because they struggled with drug use. By the time he met Dereniowski, he was working at a hospital and trying to support his family. Elvin was later identified by Puerto Rican newspaper El Nuevo Día as Elvin Chorpy Santiago. The newspaper reported on the encounter in March 2026, describing it as a social experiment that began outside a supermarket in Austin and developed into a story about generosity and faith. Its report also focused on Elvin's interaction with a mother and child after the original meeting with Dereniowski.The details of Elvin's own financial situation were central to the story. Dereniowski's published account describes him as a man who was struggling to make ends meet, yet he still chose to spend his own money on a birthday card and balloon for a stranger. That decision became the moment around which the later fundraiser was built.What happened after Dereniowski gave Elvin $1,000The first response to Elvin came directly from Dereniowski. According to Dereniowski's own account of the encounter, he gave Elvin $1,000 after learning more about his circumstances. Elvin then chose to use that money to help a mother and her child who were in need. El Nuevo Día independently reported the episode under the headline “Rechazó $1,000 para ayudar a otros”, or “He rejected $1,000 to help others”, and its article identifies Elvin as the Puerto Rican man at the centre of the encounter.That detail became another part of the story's spread online. Rather than keeping the unexpected cash for himself, Elvin was presented as choosing to direct the money towards other people who needed help. The episode also gave Dereniowski another reason to continue helping him beyond the original interaction.How Daniel Lubetzky helped turn the encounter into a larger fundraiserAfter hearing Elvin's story, Dereniowski decided that the initial gift would not be the end of the interaction. He brought in Daniel Lubetzky, the founder of KIND and a Shark Tank investor, to help take the response further. Dereniowski's published description thanks Lubetzky for supporting the campaign and specifically acknowledges his donation to help Elvin and his family.The wider effort was organised through Slingshot Giving, where viewers could contribute to the campaign. Dereniowski's description says that the community came together with Lubetzky's support and raised more than $200,000 for Elvin and his family. The figure therefore represents the wider fundraising effort, rather than a claim that Lubetzky personally gave Elvin $200,000.How a few dollars spent on a stranger became a six-figure fundraiserThe story spread because the original gesture was small compared with what followed. Elvin had stopped for someone sitting alone with a birthday cake, spent his own money on a card and balloon, returned to sing Happy Birthday and prayed for a complete stranger. He did this while dealing with his own financial difficulties and working to support his family.Dereniowski's video turned that brief encounter into a much larger campaign. The April 8 video had accumulated millions of views by September, helping bring attention to the fundraiser and Elvin's circumstances. The campaign ultimately crossed the $200,000 mark, providing financial support for Elvin and his family.What began outside an Austin grocery store therefore became a much larger online fundraising effort. The amount raised was far removed from the money Elvin originally spent, but the campaign remained centred on the same moment that started the story: a man with limited resources choosing to spend some of his own money to make a stranger's birthday feel less lonely.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UPI: The small fee raising big questions for India's payments revolution
articles.summary: Since its launch in 2016, UPI has become a central part of India's digital payments economy.
articles.body:
India's decision to introduce a fee on some transactions made through its widely popular digital payments system has sparked a debate over its impact on businesses.

The National Payments Corporation of India said on Tuesday that a 0.4% fee will apply from 15 October to certain UPI (Unified Payments Interface) payments above 2,000 rupees (£15; $21) made to businesses by customers.

Businesses will have to pay the fee and will not be allowed to pass on the cost to consumers, it said.

The government says the new charge will help keep UPI viable in the long run but experts worry it could raise expenses for businesses and discourage them from using the system.

Launched in 2016, UPI allows people to instantly send and receive money through mobile apps. The ease of use has made it integral part of everyday life in India, used by everyone - from small vendors to booming businesses.

Until now, the government, banks and payment companies have largely borne the cost of running and expanding the UPI system.

The new charge - known as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) - is expected to help cover some of those costs.

The government has said that MDR is not a tax or a charge collected by the government or NPCI, which operates the UPI system.

The money will be distributed among payment system providers - including banks - to support operations and continued expansion, the finance ministry press release stated.

The charge will not apply to all UPI payments.

Person-to-person transfers will remain free, regardless of the amount. Payments of up to 2,000 rupees made to merchants will also remain free. Merchant payments through QR codes in rural and semi-urban areas will not attract MDR either.

The government said "approximately 96% of person-to-merchant transactions will remain unaffected", either because they are below the threshold or because they are covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants.

Certain merchant payments above 2,000 rupees, including those for railways, telecom services, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will instead attract a flat charge of five rupees.

For other transactions above 2,000 rupees that are subject to MDR, the fee will be 0.4% and capped at 300 rupees per transaction. The cap applies to transactions of 75,000 rupees or more.

The regulator has said the money will support investment in areas including payment infrastructure, resilience, innovation and cyber security.

The decision has sparked debate in India.

Some social media users have said charging merchants could weaken one of UPI's biggest attractions - that it has been free to use. Others have warned that some merchants could turn to cash for larger transactions rather than absorb a fee they did not previously have to pay.

Krishnamurthy Subramanian, a former chief economic adviser to the Indian government, said the economics of a system such as UPI cannot be "evaluated using private cost versus private benefit".

Speaking to news channel CNN-News18, Indian entrepreneur and former managing director and co-founder of fintech platform BharatPe, Ashneer Grover said that there can be a possibility where "a shopkeeper could simply refuse to accept a UPI payment of 2,000 rupees and ask you to pay entirely in cash. Then you will go back to using cash".

The Retailers Association of India (RAI) has said that the charge could "undo years of progress in digital payment adoption among India's smallest retailers".

"During the festive season, a large share of transactions crosses the 2,000 rupees mark, and the moment a fee attaches itself to digital payment, cash becomes the path of least resistance," Kumar Rajagopalan, the association's CEO said.

Others argue that a fee is needed to help fund and expand the payments system.

"When government funds the subsidies paid for UPI, that amount comes from tax payers' pocket. Moving to market-linked pricing mechanism removes this tax burden and directly links the cost to large businesses which benefit from UPI," said Bipin Preet Singh, CEO of fintech firm MobiKwik.

Since its launch a decade ago, UPI has become a central part of India's digital payments economy. In August, UPI processed a record 24.51 billion transactions worth 29.82 trillion rupees (roughly $311bn), according to NPCI data.

The question now is whether the new charges will change how businesses use UPI, particularly for larger payments.

articles.title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci faces verdict for alleged war crimes
articles.summary: Prosecutors have requested a 45-year jail sentence for Thaci and three wartime commanders accused of war crimes.
articles.body:
The Kosovo war crimes tribunal will on Wednesday deliver its verdicts in the case of former President Hashim Thaci and several wartime commanders accused of murder and torture during the self-declared republic’s break from Serbia.

Thaci, 58, is facing several counts of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, torture and persecution, along with three former commanders from the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), a separatist militia that fought Serbian troops.

Thaci and the other former high-ranking commanders, Jakup Krasniqi, Rexhep Selimi and Kadri Veseli, deny the charges.

Prosecutors have requested 45-year prison sentences for each of the men.

The case is extremely contentious within Kosovo, where Thaci remains a revered figure for many Kosovan Albanians due to his role in the 1998-99 independence war.

On Saturday, tens of thousands gathered in the capital, Pristina, to call for their acquittal in the latest of several rallies since the trial began. Portraits of the four former KLA fighters have been plastered across the city along with a huge digital clock counting down to the verdicts.

“In the name of the people, declare them innocent,” one banner read.

According to prosecutors, the men targeted political opponents and civilians perceived as collaborators and traitors during their time in the KLA.

Thaci’s lawyers argued in February there is no evidence that directly links him to any of the crimes.

“There are no orders in the record from Thaci to perpetrators of crimes. There are no reports from perpetrators of crimes to Thaci,” lawyer Luka Misetic told judges at the Kosovo tribunal in February.

Most of the 13,000 people who died in the war in Kosovo were ethnic Albanians. A 78-day campaign of NATO air attacks against Serbian forces ended the fighting. About one million ethnic Albanian Kosovars were driven from their homes.

In 2008, Kosovo declared its independence from Serbia, a move that Belgrade refuses to recognise. Ties between Kosovo and Serbia remain tense, despite years of negotiations mediated by the European Union.

articles.title: In 1980, an 8-year-old found $5,800 of D.B. Cooper’s ransom money buried in Columbia River sand; 28 years later, the decayed $20 bills sold for more than $37,000
articles.summary: US News: In February 1980, eight-year-old Brian Ingram discovered packets of $20 bills tied to D.B. Cooper's infamous hijacking. This article explores the extraordinary find, the investigation that followed, and the surprising auction sale decades later.
articles.body: Eight-year-old Brian Ingram was raking sand for a family campfire on the Washington side of the Columbia River on February 10, 1980, when he uncovered three deteriorating packets of $20 bills. The money had been part of the $200,000 ransom paid to the hijacker known as D.B. Cooper in 1971, and the total value of the recovered bills was $5,800.Ingram was picnicking with his parents and relatives at Tena Bar in Clark County when he found the money buried several inches to several feet below the sand. Some bills were black or almost unreadable, while others had deteriorated to pieces. The family initially did not know whether the money was genuine.Investigators compared the serial numbers with records made by Seattle First National Bank before the ransom was handed over to Cooper. The bureau confirmed that the bills came from three ransom packets; two containing 100 $20 bills and another containing 90. The packets had originally been given to Cooper after he hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 on November 24, 1971. The discovery was the first confirmed piece of Cooper’s ransom found since the hijacking, and also produced a new question that investigators could not answer: how had part of the money travelled from wherever Cooper lost it to a sandbar along the Columbia River?The FBI could not establish how the money arrivedInvestigators searched the area after the discovery and found additional fragments, with some being several feet beneath the sand. The FBI brought in a backhoe along with specialists in soil, archaeology and river currents to examine the site. The paper had spent years exposed to water and sediment, and the original packaging was gone. FBI investigators considered the possibility that the ransom had reached the site through water movement rather than being deliberately buried there.HistoryLink’s account notes that the FBI never established with certainty how the money reached the riverbank. One theory was that a bag containing the ransom had been carried downstream before breaking apart, while former FBI agent Ralph Himmelsbach believed that the bag may have been close to a stream and later moved by high water before deteriorating.Tena Bar was on the Washington side of the Columbia, while Cooper’s exact landing point after he jumped from the aircraft was never determined. He had left the plane somewhere over southwestern Washington during the night of the hijacking. The ransom had been assembled in $20 bills because investigators wanted to make the money heavy enough to make the escape more difficult. Cooper received the cash along with four parachutes and ordered the plane toward Mexico, and then disappeared from the aircraft during the flight.The damaged bills became collectiblesThe FBI, Ingram’s family, Northwest Orient Airlines and the airline’s insurer all had claims connected to the bills. In 1986, a proposed court judgment divided the proceeds between the parties, with the FBI retaining a small amount as evidence and Ingram receiving a share. The money stayed with Ingram for years, and by 2006, he was preparing to sell portions of the collection. He eventually selected PCGS Currency to authenticate the bills before an auction.15 of the recovered bills were sold through Heritage Auction Galleries in Dallas for $37,000 in September 2008, according to HistoryLink’s account. The sale price was two to three times higher than expected, and some of the notes still carried initials made by investigators who had examined them after the discovery. Many of the original notes were too badly damaged to retain much physical integrity, and the recovered money had already been divided through the earlier legal settlement.The FBI ended its active investigation in 2016 after more than four decades of searching for the hijacker, but the Columbia River money remains one of the clearest physical links to the ransom. The bills that an eight-year-old pulled from the sand in 1980 were severely damaged yet some survived long enough to become auction pieces nearly three decades later.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: China warns U.S. space weapons could fuel arms race
articles.summary: China urged the United States to halt its military buildup in outer space after Washington acknowledged it has weapons deployed in orbit, while Chinese state media warned the move could fuel a global arms race.
articles.body: BEIJING — China urged the United States to halt its military buildup in outer space after Washington acknowledged it has weapons deployed in orbit, while Chinese state media warned the move could fuel a global arms race. Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing opposed the weaponization of outer space and turning it into a war zone. “We urge the U.S. to stop expanding military buildup in outer space, and uphold global strategic stability with concrete actions,” Guo told a regular news briefing on Tuesday. U.S. Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said Monday that the United States had “on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action,” the strongest acknowledgment yet by a Pentagon official of U.S. weapons in orbit. Meink did not identify the weapons. China’s state-backed Global Times said in a report Tuesday that the disclosure exposed what it called Washington’s pursuit of “space hegemony” and risked fueling a global space arms race. Chinese military analyst Song Zhongping told the newspaper the acknowledgment marked a shift from protecting space assets and relying on ground-based counter-space systems toward directly deploying weapons in orbit. “If the U.S. continues down this path, other countries may be forced to respond,” Song said. Last week, state news agency Xinhua said in an analysis of a U.S. orbital military exercise that Washington’s push to weaponize this domain risked creating a “security dilemma,” forcing other countries to strengthen counter-space capabilities that the United States would then regard as new threats.

articles.title: At least 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses
articles.summary: Dozens of people are missing beneath the rubble of a building hit by an Israeli strike last year, where some 10 families had been living.
articles.body:
At least 21 people have been killed, including eight children, and dozens are missing after a war-damaged building collapsed in the Gaza Strip overnight, local rescuers and medics say.

Witnesses told the BBC that the six-storey building in the Tal al-Hawa area of Gaza City had been left tilting dangerously to one side after an Israeli strike more than a year ago. Displaced families were living inside because they were desperate, they said.

UN agencies and an Egyptian team have joined the search for survivors, but officials say it is proceeding slowly due to a lack of equipment.

In the initial rescue effort, members of the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency resorted to using their bare hands.

"We are still hearing voices from under the rubble, so there is still hope to find people," said Raed al-Dahshan, the director of the Civil Defence in Gaza City.

He added: "The limited availability of shelter options forced residents to move into this building, believing it was safe. However, at one point it collapsed entirely, tragically crashing down on people as they slept."

A woman living in a tent nearby, Umm Mohammed Bakrun, said she had been talking to her son when the building collapsed suddenly in the early hours of Wednesday.

"It felt like an earthquake. There was a loud sound and I couldn't stand up. Stones rained down on us and when I looked outside I saw a lot of dust," she told the BBC. "Within minutes, there were screams everywhere."

Another witness, Mansour Abu Mohammed, said the building collapsed "in a few seconds".

"Every day, a stone or a few stones would fall from it, but the people inside couldn't find anywhere else to live. I used to live next door to it and you could see that it was tilting to one side."

Locals said some 10 families had been living in the building's apartments.

The head of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Gaza office, Alessandro Mrakic, told reporters at the scene that between 70 and 100 people were believed to be trapped under the rubble.

"The situation, as you see, is tragic because we don't have the equipment and machinery that is needed. There are actually people digging with their bare hands," he said.

Mrakic also warned that approximately 400 other war-damaged buildings across Gaza were at imminent risk of collapse, particularly as winter approaches.

"We need support, most importantly with machinery, equipment, among others. Our colleagues here don't have [engine] oil and spare parts to continue to work with all the equipment that is still in Gaza."

The UN's humanitarian relief co-ordinator, Ramiz Alakbarov, said he was "devastated" by the reports of the building collapse.

"No-one should have to risk their life simply to find a safe place to shelter," he said.

He also urged Israeli authorities to approve deliveries to Gaza of heavy machinery for rescue operations, as well as tents, tarpaulins and other non-food items for displaced people ahead of the winter rains.

Israel says its restrictions are meant to keep equipment out of the hands of Palestinian armed groups that could also have military uses.

An estimated 80% of all structures in Gaza have been destroyed or damaged during the war between Israel and Hamas, according to the UN.

More than 1.9 million people - about 90% of the territory's population - have been displaced, many of them multiple times, and 1.2 million of them are currently living in tents or makeshift shelters, it says.

The UN has warned that the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire despite the ceasefire agreed last October, as Israeli air strikes and other attacks continue to hit populated areas, causing casualties and property damage and driving further displacement.

On Tuesday, Israeli air strikes killed at least five Palestinians, including two children and a Hamas commander, according to health officials and Hamas sources.

The Israeli military said it killed a Hamas commander in southern Gaza and another fighter in the north. In both cases, a child was also reportedly killed.

Separately, the British charity Medical Aid for Palestinians said that a patient was killed by an Israeli drone at a health centre it supports in Jabalia in northern Gaza. A spokesperson for the Israeli military told the BBC it was not aware of such an incident.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 73,790 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

articles.title: In 2012, bubbles, tremors and a diesel smell appeared in a Louisiana swamp; days later, the ground opened into a lake that eventually covered 37 acres
articles.summary: US News: In 2012, residents near Bayou Corne reported mysterious bubbles and tremors, leading to the sudden formation of a massive sinkhole that expanded into a 37-acre lake, forever changing the landscape and impacting local communities.
articles.body: Residents around Bayou Corne in southern Louisiana had been reporting bubbles in the water and tremors that couldn’t be explained for weeks when a wooded section of swamp suddenly collapsed on August 3, 2012. A slurry-filled depression appeared where trees had stood, and the newly formed sinkhole began pulling water and surrounding ground toward it. Louisiana's Department of Energy and Natural Resources records show that state and federal agencies were investigating unexplained bubbling in Bayou Corne and nearby Grand Bayou during June and July 2012. On August 3, an area of wooded swamp began to subside, which prompted the state's commissioner of conservation to declare an emergency.Reports from the area described shaking beneath homes and bubbles rising through the bayou, and by late July, the frequency of the tremors had increased sharply. On the morning before the collapse, residents also reported a strong diesel-like smell, and a later aerial survey detected a diesel sheen on the surface of the slurry area, while gas continued bubbling through the water.The signs came before the collapseBayou Corne sits above the Napoleonville Salt Dome, which is a large underground salt formation that had been used for solution mining. The cavern that was involved in the incident was operated by Texas Brine, and investigations eventually linked the collapse to a breach along the side of the underground salt cavern. As material from the surrounding formation moved into the cavity, the ground above lost support.A Louisiana Transportation Research Center report later documented the event as a major subsidence episode that involved surface instability, horizontal displacement and seismic activity. The sinkhole formed about 1,500 feet south of Louisiana Highway 70, and the continuing ground movement created concerns for roads and other infrastructure in the area.The first opening was much smaller than the body of water that exists there today, and as the collapse continued, trees and marshland disappeared into the depression. Water from surrounding wetlands flowed toward the opening, while methane and other gases emerged from the area. Louisiana's incident record shows that the state emergency was declared on August 3, which was the same day the wooded area began to collapse. The evacuation eventually affected hundreds of people living near the sinkhole.From a swamp collapse to a permanent lakeContemporary measurements documented rapid growth during the first two years, while later accounts put the final surface area at roughly 37 acres. The 2024 technical account from the Solution Mining Research Institute says the sinkhole eventually reached about 37 acres, or roughly 15 hectares, as trees, shrubs and marshland fell into the expanding depression. The report also describes numerous gas-and-water bubble sites that appeared around the area after the collapse.State officials monitored methane and other emissions, while efforts were made to manage gas escaping from the underground system. Louisiana's Department of Energy and Natural Resources reported that an aerial survey detected the diesel sheen responsible for continued reports of a fuel-like odor, and the same survey found bubbling natural gas around the affected area.Something that had been a wooded swamp eventually became an expanding body of water surrounded by damaged vegetation and unstable ground. The collapse also altered how residents viewed the area around their homes. Roads, property and evacuation routes became part of a problem that could not be solved simply by filling the original hole. The mandatory evacuation was eventually lifted in 2016, but the community never returned to its pre-2012 population. The sinkhole itself remained as a large water-filled depression in the Louisiana landscape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 9-year-old boy spent his father’s $118,000 on YouTube ads promoting his Minecraft and Roblox videos
articles.summary: US News: A nine-year-old boy who runs the YouTube channel Mighty Mike Plays allegedly spent about $118,000 on YouTube advertising to promote his Minecraft and .
articles.body: A nine-year-old boy who runs the YouTube channel Mighty Mike Plays allegedly spent about $118,000 on YouTube advertising to promote his Minecraft and Roblox videos, according to his father, Dave. The situation reportedly began with a much smaller $20 advertising campaign that Dave helped his son create after the boy became frustrated with the number of views his videos were receiving. The company credit card was already saved to the Google account, allowing Mike to launch additional advertising campaigns. Dave said the spending continued for around three weeks before his employer discovered the charges. The boy reportedly believed that spending more money would result in more views for his videos, turning a small promotional experiment into a huge advertising bill.How a 9-year-old spent $118,000 promoting YouTube videosAccording to Dave, Mike wanted to attract more viewers to his gaming channel and was disappointed that his Minecraft and Roblox videos were not receiving enough attention. His father initially helped him set up a $20 YouTube advertising campaign to promote one of the videos.The campaign was intended to be a small experiment. However, Mike later continued creating advertising campaigns. Dave said his son apparently misunderstood how the advertising budget worked and believed that putting more money behind the videos would generate more views.Because payment information was already available through the Google account, the additional campaigns could reportedly be charged to the saved company card.The advertising spending continued for three weeksThe advertising reportedly continued for approximately three weeks before the company discovered the charges.During that period, Mike's videos were promoted to YouTube users as advertisements. The promoted content included videos featuring Minecraft and Roblox, the two games that form a major part of the Mighty Mike Plays channel.Dave reportedly said some of the videos received around 200,000 views after being promoted. The increased exposure, however, came at a huge cost compared with the original $20 campaign.The total advertising expenditure was eventually reported by Dave to be approximately $118,000.His father’s company discovered the chargesThe situation came to light after Dave's employer noticed the unusual charges on the company credit card.Dave said he was called into a meeting with company management and finance personnel, where the advertising expenditure was discussed. He was reportedly shown the charges accumulated over the previous weeks.The discovery left Dave facing uncertainty about what would happen next. He said he did not know whether the company would ask him to repay the money or what consequences he could face at work.There has been no reported confirmation that Dave has lost his job or that his employer has formally required him to repay the entire amount.Mike reportedly thought more spending meant more viewsThe incident appears to have stemmed from a misunderstanding about online advertising rather than an understanding of the enormous financial consequences involved.Dave explained that Mike believed spending more money would lead to more people watching his videos. For a child focused on views, subscribers and gaming content, the connection between advertising expenditure and audience growth may have seemed straightforward.But the advertising system was connected to a company payment method, creating the possibility of charges far beyond the original $20 experiment.After learning about the potential consequences for his father, Mike reportedly said he was "definitely cooked", a reaction that became one of the most widely shared details of the story.The family may pause Mighty Mike PlaysThe family has discussed pausing the channel while they deal with the situation and reconsider how the account is managed.Dave has said that stronger safeguards will be introduced, including spending limits and parental controls. Removing saved payment information is also expected to prevent a similar situation from happening again.The incident has also drawn attention because viewers had reportedly encountered unusually long Mighty Mike Plays videos being shown as YouTube advertisements. Reports from viewers described lengthy Minecraft and Roblox videos appearing as promotional content.Mighty Mike Plays has built an audience around gaming content, particularly Minecraft and Roblox. The reported advertising campaign appears to have significantly increased the exposure of some videos, but at a cost vastly greater than the original campaign.For the family, the episode began with an attempt to spend $20 to help a nine-year-old get more views. articles.title: Saudi Arabia says it shot down Houthi drone south of Mecca
articles.summary: The Houthis deny targeting the Islamic holy city after the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen accuses them of a "disgraceful act".
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of the Islamic holy city of Mecca on Tuesday evening, according to the spokesman of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen.

Turki al-Maliki said the targeting of Mecca, which is the home of Islam's most sacred shrine and the focal point of the Hajj pilgrimage, was a "disgraceful act".

The 57-nation Organisation of Islamic Cooperation said attacks on Mecca and Medina province, where Islam's second holiest shrine is located, constituted an "unacceptable and intolerable transgression".

But the Houthis, an Iran-backed armed group that controls much of western Yemen, denied targeting Mecca and accused Saudi Arabia of "fabrications and lies".

"There is no threat whatsoever from Yemen to the holy sites. Our operations target their oil facilities and military bases, and are far removed from the holy places," military spokesman Yahya Sarea said.

Sarea added that the Houthis had launched drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia in retaliation for more than 450 Saudi air strikes on their territory over the past week.

He also said they had shot down a Saudi fighter jet over Marib province.

There was no immediate response from the Saudi-led coalition, but Maj Gen Maliki did say that its forces would "not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures against the terrorist Houthi militia and its hostile and terrorist behaviour".

On Tuesday, Saudi authorities issued a series of brief security alerts for incoming projectiles in a number of western areas, including Mecca and Jeddah, the kingdom's second largest city.

Meanwhile, the US embassy in Saudi Arabia issued a "reconsider travel" advisory, warning that Houthi attacks had targeted cities, infrastructure, airports, military bases, diplomatic facilities and energy facilities.

The Houthis have recently seized control of large swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast from Saudi-backed pro-government forces.

Last week, they captured the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the southern gateway to a key shipping route that links Asia and Europe via the Red Sea and the Suez canal.

The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping but reiterated that they would target vessels from Saudi Arabia, which has relied on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

At the same time, Saudi Arabia's key East-West Pipeline, which was being used to transfer crude oil from the Gulf to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, had to be closed after it was badly damaged in a strike that the kingdom blamed on Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

Some experts have said it could take more than a month to repair the pipeline, but US Energy Secretary Chris Wright predicted on Tuesday that oil should be flowing through it within days.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the country's de facto ruler, has personally pressed US President Donald Trump to take military action against the Houthis, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News, the BBC's US media partner.

Trump has so far declined to involve the US military directly, offering instead to assist with intelligence and targeting support, the sources said.

A senior Trump administration official told the BBC: "We are in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability."

The United Nations Security Council held an emergency meeting on Tuesday, during which both Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia called for more decisive action against the Houthis, who they accused of choking the Bab al-Mandab Strait as a way of applying economic pressure.

Council members agreed that freedom of navigation in the Red Sea must be maintained to prevent disruption to global supply chains.

More than 90,000 people have been displaced in Yemen by the fighting between the Houthis and pro-government forces, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

"Families are being forced to flee for the second or third time in this conflict, with almost nothing left," Amy Pope, the IOM's director general, warned last week.

The World Health Organization (WHO) said on Sunday that at least 500 people had been reported killed since the start of August, including 297 over the previous week.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

articles.title: Japan is hosting a sleeping competition with a ₹13 lakh prize; here’s how contestants will be judged
articles.summary: Rest of World News: What if falling asleep could win you a cash prize? In Japan, a new competition is putting an unusual skill to the test: sleeping. Contestants will tak.
articles.body: What if falling asleep could win you a cash prize? In Japan, a new competition is putting an unusual skill to the test: sleeping. Contestants will take part in a 90-minute sleep competition, with a top prize of ¥2.22 million, or around ₹13 lakh. The unusual event is attracting attention for turning something as ordinary as sleeping into a competitive challenge. But this is not simply about who can close their eyes and stay in bed the longest. The tournament will assess how participants sleep and whether they can remain asleep when unexpected disturbances are introduced.Japan's 'Mattrace by Koala' to take place in OctoberThe event, called “Mattrace by Koala,” is being organised by Japanese mattress company Koala Japan. According to Tokyo Weekender, the sleep race is scheduled for October 5, 2026, at Share Green Minami Aoyama in Tokyo's Minato ward. The competition will feature three 90-minute races held throughout the day. Each race is expected to have around 20 participants. If the number of applicants exceeds the available spots, participants will be selected through a lottery. Applications opened on September 4 and are scheduled to close on September 16 at 11:59 pm (Japan time). The event was announced by Koala Japan on September 4.How the sleeping competition will workContestants will lie down on Koala mattresses and try to get the best sleep possible during the 90-minute race. However, the winner will not necessarily be the person who falls asleep first or sleeps for the entire duration. Participants will be assessed using a sleep score that considers several aspects of their rest. According to Tokyo Weekender, these include: Sleep depth, overall sleep quality, how quickly contestants fall asleep and stability of their sleep.Contestants will wear sleep-monitoring equipment during the competition. The scoring will be supervised by physicians, with the highest overall score determining the grand prize winner.The catch: Organisers will disturb contestantsThere is one unusual condition that makes this more than an ordinary nap. Organisers plan to introduce unexpected disturbances while contestants are sleeping. The idea is to see how well participants can maintain their sleep when their surroundings are not completely quiet or undisturbed. Staying asleep through these interruptions will be part of the challenge. The competition is therefore not only about falling asleep quickly. The quality and stability of sleep will also matter when the final scores are calculated.₹13 lakh prize for the best sleeperThe overall winner will receive ¥2.22 million (yen), which is approximately ₹13.76 lakh. The prize amount is linked to the “Zzz” symbol commonly associated with sleep. In addition to the main prize, the organisers have announced special awards for deep sleepers and contestants with distinctive sleeping positions.Rules contestants will have to followThe competition also has rules intended to prevent participants from deliberately manipulating their sleep performance. According to reports, contestants will not be allowed to: Stay awake all night before the competition to make themselves more tired. Deliberately arrive extremely exhausted to increase their chances of falling asleep. Use sleeping pills or similar drugs to induce sleep. Participants will also take part in light exercises before settling down for the sleep race.Why Koala is organising a sleep raceKoala Japan is presenting the event as a way to draw attention to sleep and its importance. The company, which makes mattresses, is using the competition to explore sleep quality in an unusual format. The tournament also brings attention to the difference between simply spending time in bed and achieving good-quality sleep. In this contest, falling asleep is only one part of the result. The depth, quality and stability of rest will all contribute to the final score.The first Mattrace by Koala is scheduled to take place in Tokyo on October 5.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: At least five killed in Russian drone strike near Ukraine front line
articles.summary: At least seven people also injured in attack near Nikopol in southeastern Ukraine, Dnipropetrovsk governor says.
articles.body:
Ukrainian officials say that a Russian drone strike on a bus near the front line in southern Ukraine has killed at least five people and injured seven others.

The attack on Wednesday hit an area around the city of Nikopol, Dnipropetrovsk region governor Oleksandr Hanzha said on the Telegram messaging app.

Nikopol sits on the opposite bank of the Dnipro river from the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, occupied by Russian troops since the first days of the war.

Photos posted by Ukrainian officials showed windows blown out of a white minibus, with a trail of blood streaming down the side of the vehicle.

“Russians cynically struck a passenger bus. They targeted a minibus which carried people going about their daily business,” said Mykola Lukashuk, head of the Dnipropetrovsk region council.

There was no immediate comment from Russia on the attack.

The number of civilians killed in Ukraine has increased sharply this year , according to the United Nations, amid an escalation in strikes.

At least 1,396 civilians were killed and 7,978 others wounded in Ukraine during the first six months of 2026, according to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, a 37 percent increase from the same period in the previous year.

Meanwhile, at least 250 civilians were killed and 1,596 others injured in Ukrainian attacks inside Russia during the first six months of this year, according to the UN mission, quoting credible Russian open-source reporting – a 121 percent increase in civilian casualties in the country compared with the previous year.

Both Ukraine and Russia deny deliberately targeting civilians in the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Elsewhere, an explosion was heard in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv on Wednesday morning, a witness told the Reuters news agency, while a Russian strike caused a fire at a warehouse there, city authorities said on Telegram.

Russia also attacked energy infrastructure in Ukraine’s central region of Poltava overnight into Wednesday, regional governor Vitalii Diakivnych said, without giving any further details.

A Russian drone also hit an unnamed industrial facility, Diakivnych said on Telegram.

Russia’s Defence Ministry also announced that it had hit a cargo vessel in Ukraine’s Black Sea port of Chornomorsk, in the Odesa region.

Meanwhile, one person was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Bryansk region, which borders Ukraine, the region’s acting governor Yegor Kovalchuk said in a statement on Russia’s MAX messenger app.

articles.title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'
articles.summary: Canada is seeking closer ties with EU after a breakdown in relations with the US and its president Donald Trump.
articles.body:
The president of the European Commission has backed proposals for Canada to become the EU's first "associate member".

Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Wednesday she wanted to work on "opening the door" for Canada, which would involve closer ties on various key sectors.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney last week spoke of seeking a "unique alliance" with the EU. The country currently faces tense relations with the US, compounded by an intensifying dispute over trade.

Without mentioning US President Donald Trump by name, von der Leyen said offering Canada some sort of EU membership was "not a partnership against anyone else, but for our common strength".

She added: "Partnerships are a strategic choice for Europe. But they also respond to the fracture in the international rules-based system".

Carney was in attendance at the annual key note speech in Strasbourg, and is due to address the parliament on Thursday.

Trade talks between Canada and the US collapsed last month, sparking a series of new tariff measures . Trump's repeated talk of making Canada a "51st state" has also helped to fuel the feud between the North American neighbours.

Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump

Von der Leyen told the EU's State of the Union address that the bloc and Canada "see the world with the same eyes", including on topics ranging from AI, to climate change and geopolitics.

"And we have stood together: on Ukraine, on defence, on raw materials and on supply chains. But above all... Europe and Canada believe in democracy."

She did not give specific details on how any Canadian membership would work, but listed manufacturing, technology, AI, defence, energy, critical minerals and economic security as key areas for cooperation.

Both she and other European leaders have found a reliable ally in Carney as they deal with similar problems.

In particular, they have faced Trump's aggressive use of tariffs and his threat to annex Greenland which is a sovereign territory of EU member Denmark.

But "associate membership" of the EU does not currently exist and the process, if agreed, could take years.

Earlier this year, Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz suggested - to a mixed reaction - that Ukraine could be granted this new status.

Some countries in the western Balkans including Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia are already on the long road towards full EU membership.

In Eastern Europe, Georgia and Moldova are also applying.

Ten of the bloc's 27 members are yet to ratify a free-trade agreement struck with Ottawa nearly a decade ago, and some capitals would prefer to build on existing defence and trade agreements rather than create a new form of membership for Canada.

Setting out the EU's political and policy priorities for year ahead, von der Leyen also proposed the formation of a European Security Council, which would include the UK and Ukraine, amid an ongoing threat to the continent from Russia.

"For a long time, we have discussed a leaders' format focused on the security of our continent, with partners like Canada, Norway, Ukraine, the United Kingdom and others involved," she said in the wide-ranging address.

"This is even more urgent now, given the nature and scale of the risks at play. This is why we will set out our ideas to make a European Security Council a reality."

Calls for such a body have been growing since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

It was initially a French-German conception but more countries have shown support, particularly as Trump has questioned the Nato military alliance. Other nations worry such a council could unhelpfully rival Nato.

Von der Leyen said the EU was "strengthening our work with Nato" and that expanded defence spending would be "fully aligned" with the alliance.

But at the core of such a security council would be the ability to trigger an emergency meeting if one member felt under threat, similar to Nato's Article 4.

The EU chief said it would be a "mechanism to flank" Article 4, a term that could be interpreted as complementing Nato functions or - if taken in a military context - bypassing them.

Alongside global threats, von der Leyen also said many European families were worried about the cost of living, and the "dizzying speed of change" of technology and its impacts on jobs and society.

Other proposals included inviting the world's largest AI labs for talks on how to support industry efforts to pace the frontier, as well as slashing bureaucracy for businesses in the EU.

Plans to curb social media use among children, including banning platforms for under 13s, were also put forward. Under the proposal, children aged 13 to 15 would only be able to set up social media accounts which are supervised by parents.

A new emergency tool to help countries better deal with mass migration movements following the deadly influx of migrants to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July would also be outlined.

The pledge chimes with the message of European politicians on the right and hard right who have gained support in recent years for proposing a tougher approach.

Some of them called the mass attempt to enter the EU through Ceuta an "invasion" and argued asylum rules should be suspended to deal with such a crisis.

Von der Leyen said the new emergency tool would "only be triggered under a strictly defined set of criteria" and for a specific period of time, and that fundamental rights would be protected.

Human rights groups worry such a move would see vulnerable people, including women and children, turned back and denied the protection afforded to them under international law.

articles.title: Nandy pledges crackdown on 'doxxing' after RNLI volunteers see personal details online
articles.summary: The Culture Secretary condemned how RNLI volunteers and others have had their addresses published online.
articles.body:
Lisa Nandy has vowed to strengthen the law on "doxxing" after lifeboat volunteers involved in migrant crossing rescues had their personal details published online.

The culture secretary said she would "tighten up the law" to make doxxing, which involves leaking people's home addresses, a criminal offence.

Currently, she said this kind of behaviour is only illegal if it is done with clear intent to cause fear, harm and distress.

Nandy convened a meeting with social media firms on Tuesday afternoon to discuss such abuse, but she called social media company X a "disgrace" for failing to turn up.

Last week, the chief executive of the RNLI - the Royal National Lifeboat Institute - condemned online and physical abuse volunteers for the charity had received over English Channel migrant crossings.

That followed protests after 120 people landed on Portsmouth's shores from France with the RNLI's assistance.

Nandy told BBC Breakfast she was "appalled" that the likes of RNLI volunteers, police officers, social workers and journalists were "being doxxed online" - having their names, photos and addresses published.

In her meeting with social media companies, she said she found "wildly varying standards" from them on doxxing material.

TikTok told her it would automatically remove such posts while Facebook and Instagram owner Meta said it would not, she said.

"And frankly, X didn't even bother to turn up yesterday which shows real contempt for people's safety and security and their obligations to society," she added.

She said the government "will not hesitate to take action" to make clear that "where people's addresses are being published online, that is an offence and action has to be taken swiftly".

A source close to Meta said it removes content that shares, offers or solicits personally identifiable information that could lead to physical harm.

It is undersood the Crown Prosecution Service can currently treat doxxing under offences such as malicious communications if a victim is threatened or harassed.

BBC Verify found viral social media posts about those involved in migrant crossing operations, some of which wrongly identified RNLI crew members and called for their families to be tracked down.

The RNLI has said only 109 of its 9,058 lifeboat launches last year were for people "in distress in the Channel" - 1.2% of its total rescue work.

The charity's chief executive added around 95% of small boats were intercepted by the UK Border Force.

Nandy has also taken aim at "incredibly slow" progress with enforcement of the Online Safety Act, the government's flagship law to tackle online abuse, as she called for regulator Ofcom to move faster.

Describing the "major challenges" with enforcing the Act, she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme two penalties had so far been issued to companies but no fines had yet been paid.
